chunks: And it was narrated from ʿUbaydillāh ibn ʿAlī al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام whether the testimony of Ahl al-Dhimmah is valid against those not from their religion.
He عليه السلام said: Yes. If none from the people of their own religion are found, then the testimony of others is valid. Indeed, it is not proper for the right of anyone to be lost.

key_terms.أَهْلِ ٱلذِّمَّةِ: protected non-Muslim subjects living under Islamic rule
key_terms.حَقِّ: a rightful due, claim, or legal right
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony or witness statement in a judicial context

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of Ahl al-Dhimmah accepted when witnesses from their own religion cannot be found?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the acceptance of testimony in cases involving Ahl al-Dhimmah. It establishes that when witnesses from their own religious community are unavailable, the testimony of others may be accepted so that no person's right is lost.
